text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dispute between state oil firm NNPC and ports authority yet to be resolved, keeping ships loaded with petrol waiting to dock and worsening fuel supply crisis in Lagos.
- Nigeria's population is projected at 102 million based on a rate of growth of 2.83 percent, says head of population commission Chris Ugowe at a conference in Lagos.
- Nigerian interest rates fall on increasing liquidity barely 10 days after the release of nation's fiscal budget.
- Ships from southeastern Nigeria discharge fuel in Lagos ports to end petrol crisis that has gripped the metropolis.
- Budget activates Nigerian money market, demand for foreign exchange rises to $59.5 million at latest weekly auction from less than $1 million the week before.
- Boardroom crisis looms at Nigerian Liquefied Natural Gas Company as technical leader Royal Dutch Shell Group recalls managing director Theo Oerlemans.
- Finance minister Anthony Ani sets up committee to conduct census of all businesses in Nigeria that should be subject to value added tax.
- Paterson Zochonis of Manchester Plc raises its interest in its Nigerian unit to 45.03 percent.
